# Workspace transfer (TEA to TEA export/import), and any DB model change

> Loaded when you touch `backend/app/services/workspace_io/**`, `backend/app/api/v1/workspace.py`, `backend/app/models/**`, `backend/alembic/versions/**`, … (full list in the frontmatter). Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md`; edit it here.

### Workspace Transfer (Export/Import) Conventions

The **Admin → Settings → Migration → Workspace transfer** tool (added in PR #665) moves an entire Turbo EA workspace — metamodel, configuration, settings, users, the full card inventory, relations, and 46 card-context / module tables — between Turbo EA instances as a single `.zip` bundle. It is **Turbo EA → Turbo EA** (a faithful round-trip clone), distinct from the Platform Migration importer (`platform-migration.md`), which is **third-party EA platform → Turbo EA**.

> ⚠️ **This feature serializes almost the entire database. Any DB schema change is potentially a workspace-transfer change and MUST be considered as part of that change** — otherwise the new/altered data silently fails to transfer between instances. The checklist below is mandatory whenever you touch a model or migration. There is still no CI guard that catches an un-exported table: `test_workspace_io_id_bearing_columns.py` checks the blob columns of the tables already in `ENTITY_SECTIONS`, and `test_workspace_applier_cards_exact.py` pins the order of the sheets already wired, but nothing compares `Base.metadata.tables` with the sections, so a new table that is in neither list (nor bespoke) is silently left out. The round-trip tests only cover what's already wired.

**Bundle layout** — `manifest.json` (format version, app version, timestamp, source URL, section list) + `workspace.xlsx` (one sheet per domain, the source of truth for references) + `assets/` (binary/large payloads: branding, file attachments, diagram + BPMN XML). `FORMAT_VERSION` ("1") lives in `schema.py`; bump it when the on-disk shape changes incompatibly (the importer refuses a bundle whose major version it doesn't understand).

**Module layout** (`backend/app/services/workspace_io/`):

```
workspace_io/
  __init__.py    # re-exports build_bundle / parse_bundle / apply_bundle / diff_bundle / FORMAT_VERSION
  schema.py      # FORMAT_VERSION, sheet names, the card/relation REFERENCE ENCODING (escaped parent_path),
                 #   and CONFIG_SECTIONS (declarative registry of the "simple" config tables)
  secrets.py     # SINGLE source of truth for what never leaves an instance (see below)
  exporter.py    # build_bundle() — bespoke core sheets + column-order constants (CARD_COLUMNS, …)
  applier.py     # apply_bundle() / diff_bundle() — idempotent upsert engine, dry-run via savepoint rollback
  entities.py    # generic introspection-driven export/import engine + EntitySection descriptor
  sections.py    # ENTITY_SECTIONS — the list of module/card-context tables the generic engine drives
  bundle.py      # WorkspaceBundle, zip pack/unpack, workbook (de)serialisation
  remap.py       # IdMap + the per-section rewriters that translate ids held INSIDE blobs (#1246)
```

**The bundle is built from two kinds of section:**

- **Bespoke core sections** (`exporter.py` + `applier.py`): metamodel (card/relation types), the `CONFIG_SECTIONS` tables (roles, stakeholder roles, calculations, principles, compliance regulations, resource types, card-type categories, dashboards, cost item types, license metrics, license types, custom EOL products and cycles — 13 in `schema.py`, upserted by natural key; card-type categories are exported generically but applied by the bespoke `_apply_card_type_categories` before the card types, so a built-in row on the target is never edited, and the two license sheets are exported generically but applied by the bespoke `_apply_license_catalogue` (`_BESPOKE_CONFIG_SHEETS` in `applier.py`)), tag groups/tags, users, settings, cards, card tags, relations. These need hand-written export/apply logic — built-in protection, secret stripping, the one-relation-type-per-pair rule, topological card ordering, FK remap — so their column lists are **explicit constants** (`CARD_TYPE_COLUMNS`, `RELATION_TYPE_COLUMNS`, `CARD_COLUMNS`, `RELATION_COLUMNS`, …) in `exporter.py`. Adding a column to one of these models does **not** transfer it until you add the column name to the matching constant.
- **Generic entity sections** (`entities.py`, driven by the `ENTITY_SECTIONS` descriptor list in `sections.py`): 46 card-context / module tables (stakeholders, documents, comments, todos, file attachments, card logos, diagrams + groups/favorites, BPM, PPM, GRC risks + mitigation tasks/occurrences, TurboLens compliance runs/findings, ADRs + card links/decision links/people/files, card costs, cost history, card licenses, SoAW, decision/SoAW discussions and history, saved reports, bookmarks, web portals, surveys), plus three bespoke association sheets in the same pass (`DiagramCards`, `DiagramGroupMembers`, `BookmarkShares`). Each is a small declarative `EntitySection`; **value columns are auto-derived by SQLAlchemy introspection**, so adding a plain scalar/JSON column to a covered model transfers with zero changes here. The engine runs *after* the bespoke cards section so every card FK resolves.

**Key design decisions** (don't break these):

- **Module rows preserve their source UUIDs on import; cards do not.** Cards are matched/created by the bespoke cards section (by `external_id`, then `(type, parent, name)`), so their PKs are reassigned. Every other module row keeps its original PK, so every *intra-module* FK (a task's `wbs_id`, an occurrence's `task_id`, a comment's self `parent_id`) resolves verbatim with no remap. Only three things need translation: **card FKs** (encoded `{col}__ref` + `{col}__type`, resolved via `CardResolver`), **user FKs** (encoded `{col}__email`, resolved via the email→id map — instance-local UUIDs are meaningless on the target), and **binary/large assets** (offloaded to `assets/`).
- **Idempotent upsert by natural key throughout** — re-importing the same bundle into the same instance is a true no-op (all-skip). Dry-run preview (`diff_bundle`) runs the *same* engine inside one savepoint that is rolled back, so the preview counts exactly match an apply.
- **Instance-local ids embedded in a blob are translated, never copied** ([#1246](https://github.com/vincentmakes/turbo-ea/issues/1246), fixed in 2.158.13). Cards, relations and tags land under new primary keys, so an id held *inside* a value column — a DrawIO diagram's `cardId` / `relationId`, BPMN `calledElement` / `turboea:processRef`, `called_element`, a draft flow's `draft_element_links`, a saved report's scopes and filters, survey `target_filters` and relation answers, portal / bookmark tag filters, a todo's `link`, a compliance finding's `finding_key` hash — kept pointing at the source until then, and every card on an imported diagram read as deleted. The Cards, Relations and Tags sheets carry each row's own id in `source_id` (Relations also `source_card_id` / `target_card_id`; every entity card FK a `{col}__id` beside `__ref` / `__type`); the core appliers record `source id → target id` in an `IdMap` for every row they create **or match**; and each `EntitySection` that holds ids declares a `rewrite` (`workspace_io/remap.py`, pure functions) plus its `id_bearing_columns`, run on the row's kwargs just before insert. Only an id found in the map is replaced, so a foreign BPMN process id, a pending diagram cell or a module row's preserved PK is never touched. `FORMAT_VERSION` was deliberately **not** bumped: the import check is strict equality, every reader ignores a column it does not know, and a bump would refuse every older bundle. A bundle with no `source_id` (pre-2.158.13) relinks only its diagrams, by card type + name with the bundle's own `DiagramCards` rows as the tie-break and each edge rebuilt from its two endpoints. A skipped row is **healed** — rewritten in place, counted as `updated` and `references.healed` — only when its id-bearing columns are still byte-for-byte what the bundle carries, so a same-instance re-import stays all-skip and nothing edited since is overwritten. Matching a card by `source_id` (any status, same type) is also what stopped an include-archived re-import duplicating every archived card, since the reference resolver sees ACTIVE cards only; an archived row is additionally resolved by type + path through a second `CardResolver.load(..., status="ARCHIVED")`, with reference / external id as the tie-break. The `CardTags` and `DiagramCards` sheets carry `card_id` for the same reason, and every bespoke end goes through `_card_end` (id first, reference second). A saved report's config and the survey / portal / bookmark filters are also deep-walked (`replace_mapped_ids`) over the keys nobody named, so a key a report adds later still translates — the named keys stay what counts `unresolved`. Known limit: a finding healed to a key the target's own scan already minted (import pre-fix → scan → re-import) collides with that row; the pure rewriter cannot see the table, and that instance already held both findings. Guard tests: `tests/services/test_workspace_io_id_bearing_columns.py` (every JSON / Text / binary / asset column is either declared or allowlisted with a reason), `test_workspace_io_id_remap.py` (imports into a **wiped** inventory so ids genuinely change — a canary scans every entity row for a surviving source id), `test_workspace_io_remap.py`.
- **User ids inside blobs follow their user (2.200.0).** Mention spans in a decision's four text sections, a SoAW's `sections[*].content`, a discussion comment's `body` and a history snapshot (`<span data-type="mention" data-kind="card|decision|user" data-id="…">`, grammar in `app/services/mention_markup.py`, the one module both the rewriter and the mention service use) name cards and users; signatory lists (`Adrs` / `Soaws` / `DocumentHistory.signatories`) and a snapshot's `content.people[*].user_id` name users. The Users sheet carries each user's own id in `source_id`, and `_apply_users` records `source id → target id` in `IdMap.users` for every user it creates **or matches by e-mail**, in a dry run too (`_load_remap_context` backfills it by e-mail for a selective run). Card ids go through `IdMap.cards`; decision ids are module PKs and stay. **Known limit:** a bundle written before 2.200.0 has no user `source_id`, so its user mentions and signatory ids are left as they were (counted `unresolved`) and read as an unknown person on the target. `DocumentHistory.seq` is an identity column the target assigns: the section excludes it and exports in `seq` order (`EntitySection.export_order_by`), and rows are inserted in sheet order, so the timeline keeps its order. These two sections are also the only ones that carry `created_at` (`EntitySection.carry_timestamps`: a thread's and a timeline row's date is content, where everywhere else it is the import time; an empty cell falls back to the server default) and that read an empty cell back as `""` for their NOT NULL text columns (`EntitySection.keep_empty_text`: a deleted comment and a rejection without a reason store an empty `body`, which the workbook otherwise returns as `None`).
- **Costs and licenses transfer as catalogue keys, never ids.** The catalogues are `ConfigSection`s: `CostItemTypes` (natural key `key`), `LicenseMetrics` (`key`) and `LicenseTypes` (`(metric_key, key)`; the same type key under two metrics is two rows); columns `key`, `label`, `sort_order`, `archived`, `translations` (plus `metric_key` on types). Every config section, and the license catalogue, is applied before the entity sections, so the keys the per-card rows name already exist on the target. The per-card data are three `EntitySection`s with `card_id` as their card FK (encoded `card_id__ref` / `__type` / `__id`, resolved like any other) and a `natural_key`, so a row matching one the target already has under another PK replaces its values instead of hitting the unique constraint: `CardCosts` (`card_id`, `fiscal_year`; `items` = `{item_key: {"amount", "renewal_date"}}`), `CardCostHistory` (`card_id`, `fiscal_year`, `field_key`; a past-year `value` of an Initiative / Provider cost field) and `CardLicenses` (`card_id`, `fiscal_year`; `items` = `{metric_key: {type_key: {"licensed", "actual"}}}`). Their blobs hold only keys, amounts, counts and dates, so they have no `rewrite` and are allowlisted in `ID_FREE_COLUMNS` (`test_workspace_io_id_bearing_columns.py`) with that reason; `metric_key` is a key, not an id. `CardCosts` is a **card-finalising** sheet: the applier's closing pass (`_finalize_cards`) runs `card_costs.recompute_derived` before the calculations, because a formula may read `costTotalAnnual`; `CardCostHistory` and `CardLicenses` change no card attribute and are not in that set. **Putting an id into `card_costs.items` (a provider or contract card, a relation, a tag) or into `card_licenses.items` turns that column into an id-bearing one**: drop its `ID_FREE_COLUMNS` entry, declare `id_bearing_columns=("items",)` with a `rewrite` in `remap.py` that maps through the `IdMap` (`ids.lookup(remap.CARDS, …)`, never a copied UUID), add the section to `test_the_sections_that_hold_ids_are_the_known_ones`, and prove it with a round-trip into a **wiped** inventory in `test_workspace_io_id_remap.py`. A new key that is a catalogue key needs none of that, but a new catalogue table needs its own `ConfigSection`; a new cost field that feeds a card attribute keeps `CardCosts` (or its new sheet) in the finalising set in `applier.py`. Guard tests: `test_workspace_io_cost_items.py`, `test_workspace_io_cost_history.py`, `test_workspace_io_licenses.py`, `test_workspace_io_license_catalogue.py`.
- **Legacy stakeholder cost grants.** A bundle with a `CostItemTypes` sheet uses the fork threshold (`2.208.0`); other bundles use upstream's threshold (`2.206.0`). Older bundles retain legacy grants except for Observer. An explicit `card.view_costs` value wins. For fork bundles before `2.208.0`, the same legacy-role rule applies to `card.view_licenses`. An explicit `card.view_licenses` value wins.
- **The license catalogue has its own applier, `_apply_license_catalogue`, and still imports a bundle written before license metrics.** It runs after the core sections and before the entity sections, and also when only `CardLicenses` is selected. The generic config applier is not used: it fails a row with a `None` part of its natural key and overwrites `archived` / `sort_order`. **A bundle is old when its `LicenseMetrics` sheet is absent (never merely empty) or a `LicenseTypes` row has no `metric_key` column**; `license_compat.derive_catalogue` (pure) then derives its catalogue as migration 192 does (the same `licensing_migration.derive_type_metrics`): the default metrics it lacks are added, each type goes under every metric its own `CardLicenses` holds cells for, under both defaults when none. An old bundle's metrics are only inserted, never changed, and a derived type never changes `archived` or `sort_order` of a row the target already has; selecting either license sheet of an old bundle writes both. A new-format bundle follows the config merge. A type whose metric is on neither side is reported and skipped; a `CardLicenses` cell whose `(metric, type)` exists in neither the bundle nor the target is dropped and reported on the `CardLicenses` section (`keep_known_cells`), never imported, and the applier hands the filtered rows to the entity pass by **replacing `bundle.sheets["CardLicenses"]` in place** (callers of `apply_bundle` / `apply_selected` get their bundle changed). `licensingModel` is retired: `_apply_card_types` strips it from an incoming schema (`without_model_field`) and the cards pass drops `attributes.licensingModel` on Application / IT Component; nothing restores it. `FORMAT_VERSION` did not move: the new sheets are recognised by their shape, and an older instance ignores sheets it does not know. Guard tests: `test_workspace_io_license_catalogue.py`, `test_workspace_applier_cards_exact.py` (the license sheets sit after `Relations`, before the entity sections).
- **Secrets never leave the instance.** `secrets.py` is the single source of truth: SMTP/SSO/AI credentials (`GENERAL_SECRET_PATHS` / `EMAIL_SECRET_PATHS`) are dropped, and any `enc:`-prefixed Fernet value is defensively scrubbed (it's non-portable — derived from the source instance's `SECRET_KEY`). The importer never writes a secret field back; it preserves whatever the target already has — it runs the incoming settings through the same `strip_secrets` before merging (extension secrets `ext.<key>.secret.*` are matched by key, `is_extension_secret_key`), and `_merge_settings` merges an incoming block into an empty one when the target has none rather than copying it whole, which is how a hand-edited bundle used to plant an SSO or AI secret in plain text (fixed in 2.157.3). The cards pass gives each row its own savepoint, as bulk create does, so a row refused after it was added (the depth check, a flush-time error) leaves nothing behind and cannot fail the rows after it. Synthetic (auto-created) users land **deactivated** with no password and a role clamped to `member` if their exported role is unknown.

**A bundle is parsed from its path, and its assets are read one at a time.** `parse_bundle` accepts `bytes | Path`; given a path it holds the zip open and hands back a `ZipAssetStore` (`bundle.py`) that reads a member only when asked, so a 2 GB import never has its attachments, diagram XML and branding inflated into one `dict[str, bytes]`. The bundle therefore **owns an open file** — use it as a context manager (`with parse_bundle(path) as bundle:`) around the whole diff/apply, and never `read_bytes()` the upload. A plain `dict` still satisfies the `AssetStore` protocol, which is what keeps content packs (`build_content_bundle`) and the in-memory tests working unchanged; anything iterating assets must use `.keys()` + `.get()`, never `.items()`, or it defeats the laziness. Uploads are spooled to disk in chunks (`_spool_upload_to_disk`, `MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES` = 2 GB) from a worker thread, and the parse runs in one too — it is minutes of CPU that would otherwise block the single uvicorn event loop. `open_bundle` refuses a bundle whose central directory declares an implausible member or total size (`MAX_ASSET_BYTES` / `MAX_BUNDLE_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES`) before reading a byte. The export side still builds its zip in memory — that is a known follow-up, not a pattern to copy. Guard tests: `tests/services/test_workspace_io_unit.py`, `tests/api/test_workspace_transfer_upload.py`, `tests/services/test_db_session_holding.py`.

**Checklist when you change the DB schema** (do the matching step or the data won't transfer):

1. **New module / card-context table** (something a card hangs off, or a feature's own data): add an `EntitySection` to `ENTITY_SECTIONS` in `sections.py`, in **dependency order** (intra-module parents before children). Declare its `card_fk_columns`, `user_fk_columns`, any `asset_columns` / `json_asset_columns`, and `self_parent_column`. Add a round-trip assertion to `test_workspace_io_roundtrip.py`.
2. **New config / metamodel table**: add a `ConfigSection` to `CONFIG_SECTIONS` in `schema.py` (natural key + column list, `json_columns` for its JSONB, `skip_columns` for instance-local FKs such as `created_by`), or wire bespoke logic in `exporter.py`/`applier.py` if it needs built-in protection / FK remap. Config sections are applied in tuple order, so a table another one points at by key goes first (`EolCustomProducts` before `EolCustomCycles`). A table that is instance-local on purpose (history, caches, receipts, secrets: `audit_log`, `events`, `dashboard_kpi_snapshots`, `catalogue_cache`, `extension_licenses`) says so in a comment on its model or in the `sections.py` docstring.
3. **New column on a bespoke core model** (CardType, RelationType, Card, Relation, TagGroup, User, …): add the column name to the matching `*_COLUMNS` constant in `exporter.py` (and `*_JSON` if it's JSONB). **This is the easy one to forget** — introspection does *not* cover the bespoke core sections.
4. **New column on an entity-section model**: a plain scalar/JSON column needs nothing. But if it's a **card FK**, add it to `card_fk_columns`; if a **user FK**, add it to `user_fk_columns` (instance-local UUIDs must be remapped by email, never exported raw); if **binary/large/secret**, declare it as an asset or exclude it.
5. **New secret-bearing settings path**: add it to `GENERAL_SECRET_PATHS` / `EMAIL_SECRET_PATHS` in `secrets.py`.
6. **Incompatible on-disk shape change**: bump `FORMAT_VERSION` in `schema.py`.
7. **A JSON / XML / text column that stores a card, relation or tag id** (in any shape — a list, a map, an attribute in XML, a path in a link): declare it in the section's `id_bearing_columns` and give the section a `rewrite` in `remap.py`, or allowlist it in `test_workspace_io_id_bearing_columns.py` with the reason it holds none. The guard fails until one of the two is done. Round-trip tests for it must wipe the inventory first — a same-instance re-import keeps every id and proves nothing.

**Routes** (`backend/app/api/v1/workspace.py`, prefix `/admin/workspace`): `GET /export` (streams the `.zip`, `?include_archived=`), `POST /import` (upload → background dry-run preview), `GET /import/{id}` (poll status + diff/result), `POST /import/{id}/apply` (background apply), `DELETE /import/{id}` (discard). Gated by the dedicated `admin.export_workspace` / `admin.import_workspace` permissions (in `core/permissions.py`). The async preview/apply lifecycle is tracked in the `workspace_transfers` table; the uploaded bundle binary lives on disk under `data/workspace_transfers/{id}.bin`. Frontend: `WorkspaceTransferAdmin.tsx`, surfaced as the second tab of `MigrationHub.tsx`.
